chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahbub, from Rabi' al-Asam, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a wife in al-Iraq and committed immorality while he was in al-Hijaz. He said: He shall be struck with the prescribed penalty (hadd) of the fornicator — one hundred lashes — and he shall not be stoned.

I said: But if he was with her in the same city, yet is imprisoned in a prison, unable to go out to her and she is unable to come to him — what is your view if he commits adultery in the prison? He said: He is at the status of the one absent from his wife; he shall be flogged one hundred lashes.

key_terms.الزاني: Al-zani — the fornicator/adulterer; technically the hadd for an unmarried person (jald: 100 lashes)
key_terms.بمنزلة الغائب: At the status of the absent one — the legal fiction applied here: a man imprisoned or geographically separated is treated as unmarried for purposes of the hadd
key_terms.حد: Hadd — the prescribed, fixed legal penalty under Islamic law for specific offenses, including adultery
key_terms.يجلد: Jald — flogging/lashing, the hadd for an unmarried person committing zina
key_terms.يرجم: Rajm — stoning to death, the hadd for a married person (muhsan) who commits adultery

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on the hadd penalty for a married man who commits adultery while separated from his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a key distinction in Islamic jurisprudence regarding the hadd penalty for adultery (zina): whether a married man receives the more severe stoning (rajm) or the lesser flogging (jald). The ruling is that physical separation — whether geographic distance or imprisonment — renders the man legally equivalent to an unmarried person, and he receives only one hundred lashes. The legal principle being applied is that the aggravated penalty of stoning requires the man to have had actual, unimpeded access to his wife; physical impossibility of conjugal relations removes the aggravated condition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Rabie Al Asam, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man, for him is a woman at Al-Iraq, so he committed immorality and he was at Al-Hijaz. So heasws said: ‘He would be struck with the Penalty (Hadd) of the adultery, one hundred lashes, and he would not be stoned’.

I said, ‘So if she was with him in one city, and he is imprisoned in the prison, not being able to go out to her, nor for her to come over to him. What is your<sup>asws</sup> view, if he were to commit adultery in the prison?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘He is at the status of the absentee from his wife. He would be whipped one hundred lashes’.
